title: Best Standing Desks UK
short: Electric, manual and desk-riser standing desks compared by height range, weight capacity and price.
intro: A standing desk can be a full electric frame, a simple riser that sits on your existing desk, or something in between. This guide compares desks tested by Expert Reviews, from budget risers to heavy-duty dual-motor frames, so you can match the option to your space and budget.

guide.q: Full standing desk or a riser?
guide.a: A full electric desk replaces your existing desk and usually offers the smoothest, most stable height adjustment. A riser sits on top of a desk you already own, which is cheaper and needs no assembly of a frame, but takes up desktop depth and often has a smaller working surface.

guide.q: What weight capacity do I need?
guide.a: Add up your monitor, PC, and anything else that stays on the desk. Most home office setups fit comfortably within 80kg, but a heavier dual-monitor or multi-screen setup benefits from a higher-capacity frame like the FlexiSpot E8 or Fully Jarvis.

guide.q: Are memory height presets worth having?
guide.a: If you switch between sitting and standing during the day, presets let you return to your exact preferred height with one button press, rather than adjusting each time by eye.

guide.q: How much should I stand at a standing desk?
guide.a: There is no fixed rule, but alternating between sitting and standing through the day, rather than standing continuously, is generally recommended. A sit-stand desk lets you change position gradually rather than committing to one all day.
